mechanism_narrative: The sharp four-week collapse in WORKPLACES mobility signals a broad contraction in out-of-home activity that will continue to depress retail visits over the next four weeks, because fewer commuters and errands reduce discretionary shopping trips.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than over the last 28 days while WORKPLACES remains below -40 and TRANSIT remains below -50 for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility rises above a very high confinement threshold, people substitute away from shopping trips and stay at home, so RETAIL_REC falls further within one week and stays weak for the next month.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above +30 on a weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline further within 1 week after RESIDENTIAL exceeds +30, or rebounds above the prior 4-week mean within 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall sharply at the same time, the implied mobility restriction shock reduces access to stores and suppresses retail mobility over the following two to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline further within 2 weeks after simultaneous week-on-week drops of more than 10 points in both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM combined with continued weakness in RETAIL_REC indicates trips are concentrating in essential shopping only, which will keep retail-and-recreation mobility below its recent average over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises to within 10 points of its last-4-week mean even though GROCERY_PHARM remains at or above zero.

mechanism_narrative: A large negative PARKS shock reflects fewer leisure trips and broader suppression of discretionary outings, and that same leisure contraction will spill over into retail visits with a lag of two to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -25 on a weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall further within 2 weeks after PARKS drops below -25, or rises above its prior 4-week mean within 4 weeks.

mechanism_narrative: In a strict stay-at-home regime, rising RESIDENTIAL mobility alongside falling TRANSIT indicates commuting is replaced by home confinement, which pushes retail mobility lower over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays above +25 and TRANSIT stays below -50.

mechanism_narrative: A continued week-over-week deterioration in RETAIL_REC itself will persist because consumers and merchants adjust to a new low-traffic norm, making the next four weeks weaker than the last four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC falls for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stops falling within 1 week of a second consecutive weekly decline, or the next 4-week mean exceeds the last 4-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM weakens while PARKS and TRANSIT also remain depressed, households are not substituting into local errands or outdoor activity, so retail-and-recreation mobility will keep falling over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -10 while PARKS and TRANSIT stay below -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within 2 weeks after GROCERY_PHARM falls below -10 and both PARKS and TRANSIT remain below -20.
